item.title: Evil or Helping Angel? How one librarian keeps AI honest and accurate
item.description: By Ebele Orakpo The widespread adoption of Artificial Intelligence has sparked growing concerns over its societal impact. Critics warn that heavy reliance on AI weakens critical thinking, creativity, and human mentorship in education while widening the digital divide. Also, creative industries face job displacement, copyright theft, and unauthorised likeness cloning. Digital markets are flooded with mass-produced AI content, devaluing human artistry. In this chat with Vanguard, Mr. Amed Demirhan, one of the pioneers of e-library worldwide and the General Manager/Director of the Barzani National Memorial Library and Museum in Kurdistan, Iraq, deviates from the norm of merely learning how to operate AI and advocates for training AI to maximize its output. The former Director of Library Services, American University of Nigeria, Yola, argues that this proactive approach can preserve jobs previously considered vulnerable to automation and concludes that human intelligence is still the ultimate. Excerpts: Training the AI Like many new innovations, AI sharply divides public opinion. While some praise it as an exceptional breakthrough, others view it as very dangerous, raising serious ethical concerns like information manipulation. However, I believe AI remains one of the most effective research assistants one can get. AI capabilities AI can perform complex tasks associated with human intelligence, including learning, adapting, analyzing information, problem- solving, and remembering. Within seconds, it can browse billions of global, multilingual records and resources—far exceeding the collections of the largest physical national libraries—to retrieve requested information. However, as a human creation, AI reflects all human imperfections. Just like any student, researcher, or research assistant, it requires proper training to become truly effective. Otherwise, when you ask a question or direct it to gather research information, it will retrieve overwhelming, unhelpful results, much like sailing across the vast ocean without a compass or clear direction. Set the rules Training AI with information literacy standards, including evaluating source content, verifying facts, checking author and publisher credibility, and citing properly, makes it far more effective for academic researchers. Beyond these foundational standards, we can add tailored, research-specific rules to target unique project needs. The AI operates strictly within a structured framework rather than searching randomly if instructed to retain these guidelines. My rules I rely on a strict set of principles when working with AI; I call these “my rules” because, much like students, AI does not always follow instructions automatically. Instead of constantly repeating my guidelines when requesting research, I simply tell it to follow “my rules.” Usually, it remembers the standards and corrects its output. item.title: 3-year-old girl defiled at school, expelled; mother cries for justice
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure For Mrs Usman, the day started like any other school day. Her husband went to pick up their two children from Oakland Kids Nursery and Primary School, Oda Road, Akure, not knowing that their little daughter would come home with a story that would change their family forever. It was at home that evening that the truth began to unfold. Their 3-year-old daughter, a KG II pupil, quietly told her elder brother, who is in Nursery II, that a boy in her class had touched her. How father heard Her father overheard the conversation. Worried, he called the little girl and asked her to explain. She mentioned the name of her classmate and said he touched her private part. Her father immediately called her mother. At first, Mrs. Usman thought it might be a child’s misunderstanding. But when she got home after 7pm, she checked her daughter’s pants and saw blood stains. And when the child urinated, she cried out in pain. Asked again who touched her, she repeated the same name. Asked why she did not tell her teachers, the little girl said she was afraid she would be beaten. Nightmare, search for healthcare That night, the family rushed to a nearby pharmacy. The pharmacists said they could not handle such a case and advised them to see a paediatrician. The next day, October 28, Mrs. Usman took her daughter to the Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Akure. After examination, doctors confirmed the child had been defiled. With the medical report in hand, she went straight to the school to report. ‘CCTV not working’ According to her, the proprietor expressed shock. But when she asked to see the CCTV footage of the classroom, she was told the camera was not working. She also asked that the parents of the boy be informed. She said the school did not do so until the following day, after she raised her voice. The boy’s mother, on hearing the news, was said to have queried the school for not informing her earlier. Mother’s cry Mrs. Usman said she only asked for one thing: that her daughter should not remain in the same class as the boy. Instead, she said the proprietor suggested moving her daughter to Nursery I, where she would repeat the class if she could not cope. “Why should my daughter, the victim, be the one to be moved?” she asked. The situation worsened when the boy’s father allegedly called her, accusing her of making a false allegation and threatening her, saying, don’t bite more than what you can chew.” Mrs. Usman said the proprietor later admitted the school gave the man her phone number so they could talk as parents. Police Feeling threatened, she went to the police station. She was directed to the Gender Based Violence agency in the state. She later petitioned the State Commissioner of Police. But instead of support, she said the proprietor gave her an option: withdraw the case or have both her children expelled. She refused to withdraw. item.title: Messi’s defending champions Miami knocked out of MLS Cup playoffs
item.description: Columbus Crew, with an injury-time goal from Santiago Rodriguez, beat Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami 1-0 to knock the defending champions out of the first round of the MLS Cup playoffs on Friday. Rodriguez’s goal in the second minute of stoppage time gave Columbus a 2-0 triumph in the best-of-three first-round series, after their stunning 3-0 victory in game one in Florida. The defeat was a season-ending disappointment for the star-studded Miami side that features Messi, Luis Suarez, Casemiro and Rodrigo De Paul, which also came up short in the CONCACAF Champions Cup and the Leagues Cup. For Argentine superstar Messi, MLS’s top scorer in the regular season and the favorite to win an unprecedented third straight Most Valuable Player award, it was a second first-round exit in the three MLS Cup playoffs he has contested. Miami, facing a must-win game after dropping the opener at home to seventh-seeded Columbus, had chances to score on a cold, rainy night in Ohio. German Berterame had a golden opportunity six minutes from full time, but his header from point-blank range went over the crossbar. The match appeared headed for a penalty shootout with injury time ticking away. But Inter’s defense allowed Rodriguez to bring down a cross in the box from Moroccan Anass Zaroury and blast it past Canadian goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair. Miami’s early exit extends the champion’s curse in MLS. No team has retained the title since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2012. item.title: Giving back is success secret mother taught me — Dangote
item.description: *…why I’m teaching my daughters too Following his delivery of the Keynote address themed “The Geography of Opportunity: Why the World Needs What Africa Has,” recently at the 25th anniversary conference of Women in Management, Business, and Public Service, WIMBIZ; special guest and President/Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Ltd, Aliko Dangote, GCON sat down to a historic fireside chat with Rolake Akinkugbe Filani. The chat, anchored by the CEO, EnergyInc Advisors while also fielding questions from an audience of about 2000 women, was according to him, with the largest exclusive assembly of women he has ever addressed. Excerpts:- When your IPO closed some weeks ago, we heard that you had received a hundred and twenty applications and every single one of the 54 African countries had also applied. In your mind, Africans investing in the continent, is that one example of the geography of opportunity? Yes. What we have done with this IPO is trying to do something where, when there’s an offer in Kenya Nigerians will participate. When we did the private placement the whole idea was for us to sell 2.5 billion dollars. 1 billion was for private placement, 1.5 billion was for IPO. When we rolled out the private placement we got 3.7 billion, so we took only 2.5. What we want to do is spread this prosperity. Did this particular IPO change your view on how you mobilise capital from the African continent ? It has changed dramatically. Things are really changing very fast. Even abroad, people have a change of mind about Africa. We’ve gotten amazing demand. We’re talking about millions participating. Saudi Aramco worldwide was about 5million. We didn’t reach 10 million because of time constraints. A lot of people didn’t know how to access but the sheer trust of public enterprise that we have today in Africa, that’s why people are starting to remove their money from under their mattress to come and invest. Incredible achievement. You came from a long line of women who were in commerce, your mother, your great aunt and even your step grandmother. We want to hear if there are principles you learned by watching, by trends, by conversations, from the women in your family. From my mum it’s learning how to give back. she was always talking about giving back and she in the 80s would make sure that everyday we were feeding the poor, about 12000 people, three square meals and then we gave about 35,000 loaves of bread everyday. item.title: What Pete Edochie wanted to be remembered for
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku When Vanguard encountered Pete Edochie, the Lion of Africa in his den on two different occasions, it was never just an interview.It was an audience with a king. Ebubedike sat on his throne, spoke in proverbs, laughed loudly, sipped from a glass of fresh palm wine and dropped revelations that have now become timeless. Those conversations carried the full weight of Pete Edochie and what he represented on the big screen and in real life. The first encounter was in a hotel room in Owerri, in 2015, where he displayed rare qualities that set him apart from his contemporaries: his sense of humour, his values as a father and an actor, as well as his impeccable command of the English language. The second encounter was at his Trans Ekulu, Enugu residence in 2022. During the encounter, Ebubedike was in his element. His imposing duplex dotted with images of his artistic journey, laurels and his image as the godfather of the Nigerian movie industry set the tone for the timeless conversation. When you were eventually ushered into his living room, you were bound to appreciate why Chinua Achebe preferred to call him ‘Ebubedike’ after the iconic role he played as Okonkwo in the NTA adaptation of the classic novel, ‘Things Fall Apart.’ The Lion of Africa roared as he sat on his throne, “You are welcome to my home, feel comfortable.” Indeed, Pete Edochie was inseparable from his movie characters. In real life, he was a man of honour and class. When you were with him, you would not be tired of laughing. Intermittently, he would smile to encourage his guests while sharing his story passionately with them. As we recount those encounters spanning our august visit to him in Enugu in 2022, his repeated battles with rumours of his death, his reflections on Nollywood, family and mortality, now read like a final testament after his death on Wednesday, due to prolonged battle with prostate cancer. His love for classical music Beyond acting, Pete Edochie was an ardent lover of classical music and once presented a programme called ‘Music from the Masters’ while working as a broadcaster with Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Corporation, ENBC and the Anambra State Broadcasting Service. Recalling how he developed the passion for classical music, the movie legend revealed that his wife influenced his interest in classical music. “My wife influenced me. She was very fond of classical music. When I met her she looked me in the face and said: ‘there’s something you don’t know about yourself, you are deeper than you think. You are very emotional, I see you with your friends expressing yourselves at a social gathering. But deep down, you are a very serious person’. “One day, she joined me in the preview room, where we played some classical music. At one point, when we were playing some aspects of Mozart’s songs, I got drawn into it, forcing me to go back to play it again. Before I knew what was happening, it stuck,” he told Vanguard. item.title: Uduere Killings in Delta: Six trucks of policemen, yet bullets still found targets
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi The sound of gunfire shattered the campaign atmosphere at Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, November 23. People who had gathered for a political rally suddenly scrambled for safety. Women ran, campaigners scattered and, in the ensuing chaos, bullets found human targets. By the time the shooting stopped, families had lost loved ones, several people critically wounded and communities plunged into mourning. Among the disturbing details was that six truckloads of policemen had reportedly been deployed to provide security. Former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, put their number at close to 50. Yet, according to accounts from both political camps, the violence escalated despite the robust security presence. The tragedy has since generated competing accusations between the All Progressives Congress, APC, and the National Democratic Congress, NDC. Beneath the political blame game are grieving families, wounded survivors and ordinary citizens asking why a political gathering should become a death trap. A Trail Of Troubled Political Gatherings Uduere was not an isolated incident in the build-up to Delta 2027 elections. September 18, a one-million-man march organised by the NDC in the Warri-Effurun axis was disrupted by violence, leaving persons wounded. An AK-47 allegedly recovered from a suspect identified as Collins became a subject of controversy between the party and police. The NDC alleged the suspect was released the following day, a claim that formed part of its subsequent complaints about police handling of the incident. October 3, the party held a 10,000-man march against hunger in Ughelli. The following day, the Ughelli North Local Government Council, chaired by Chief Jaro Egbo, issued a notice, sealed the business premises and impounded truck belonging to Tobore Alex Agbah, who led the march. Agbah would later become one of the victims of the Uduere violence. November 7, another NDC one-million-man march in Asaba ended in violence, with one fatality recorded. The recurrence of disturbances has fuelled allegations that NDC gatherings are being targeted by political opponents allegedly linked to the ruling APC. Delta State Commissioner for Information, Charles Aniagwu, however, rejected the suggestion of a pattern. “It’s not a pattern, because when you talk about a pattern, it means that it’s continuously and then you are linking it to be able to join one to the other,” he said. He argued: “The NDC is not being attacked, there are a number of local governments where we have not had any disturbances. The APC in Delta is holding sway, the underdogs in this case are the members of the NDC who are few.” But NDC governorship candidate, Chris Iyovwaye, disagreed, recalling the September incident. “Another thug of APC was caught with an AK-47 and was handed over to the police. item.title: How Tinubu fought Obasanjo to reclaim Lagos coastline – Fashola
item.description: By Juliet Umeh As the 2027 general elections draw closer, political defections, shifting alliances and questions about leadership are beginning to shape the debate over who should govern Nigeria for another four years. But for former Lagos State Governor, Mr Babatunde Fashola, one important test for anyone seeking to lead the country is the ability to build relationships, work with others and remain committed to a political team, even in difficult times. Fashola believes President Bola Tinubu has demonstrated these qualities, arguing that his ability to retain political associates and bring former opponents into his camp makes him better placed to manage Nigeria’s diversity. In a pointed challenge to opposition leaders, the former governor asked voters to examine what happened to the people who worked with other presidential contenders and why many of them were no longer in their political camps. Speaking during an interview on Arise Television, Fashola said political relationships should serve as a reference point for assessing the leadership capacity of those seeking the presidency. “Where are all the people who worked with them today? That’s a job reference question. For those who want to vote, where are all the people who worked with these people? Why is it only President Tinubu that has all those who worked with him when he was governor still with him? And they were with him for 16 years or so, out of office, when he wasn’t a president,” he said. According to him, the ability to work with people is essential for anyone entrusted with managing a country as diverse as Nigeria. “If you are going to get entrusted with managing Nigeria’s diverse family, you must be able to work in a team. And you don’t just get up and jump away when there’s a crisis in the fold,” he said. Fashola noted that Tinubu remained in the All Progressives Congress, APC, despite internal disagreements, while some political leaders had abandoned parties that helped build their political careers. He also pointed to Tinubu’s ability to bring former opponents into his political fold, describing it as evidence of his capacity to build relationships across political divides. “Not just those who worked with him before, those who opposed him are now working with him. That’s how he has built a coalition of 30 state governors from one state, from Lagos. And that is profound, whether you like him or not,” he said. Why I refused to join another party Fashola’s argument about political loyalty also reflects his own experience as Lagos governor, when he said he resisted pressure to abandon his political platform in exchange for certain benefits from the Federal Government. He recalled that during a meeting with a former President, an unnamed governor suggested that Lagos would only regain access to Lagos House, Marina, if he joined the ruling party at the time. item.title: INEC tests BVAS, result portal today
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, will today run a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), about seven weeks before the 2027 general election. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser, ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. He said the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal, IReV, v,lidation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on 16 January 2027 across 177,299 polling units, with governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections to follow on 6 February 2027. Amupitan said the Commission had procured new accreditation machines and set a lower voter threshold for the actual election in January. “INEC will deploy over 1.41 million ad hoc personnel alongside 57,000 newly procured Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices, calibrated at a reduced threshold of 850 voters per machine,” he said. He told the gathering that the rehearsal was as much a test of coordination with security agencies as of technology. “Strategy without rehearsal is merely aspiration,” he said. The INEC chairman called on the Commission’s Resident Electoral Commissioners and the Commissioners of Police in the states to take part fully. “I urge all Resident Electoral Commissioners and Commissioners of Police to treat November 28 as a full-scale operational rehearsal: test your communication lines, evaluate rapid-response times around mock polling centres, and identify any logistical or security blind spots while there is still ample time to resolve them,” he said. INEC had earlier published the list of polling units selected for the nationwide mock accreditation exercise, naming 17,656 locations across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory FCT. The commission said the exercise is a “Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise” using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS. The list gives the state, local government area, ward, polling unit and delimitation code of each selected location. It runs alphabetically from Abia State to Zamfara State, with the FCT last. Abia has 368 entries, while Adamawa follows with 452. In the FCT, 124 polling units were selected across the six area councils. Abaji, Bwari, Gwagwalada, Kuje and Kwali have 20 each, while the Municipal Area Council has 24. item.title: Death on the River: Some who came for rescue were more interested in stealing phones, bags, money — Survivor
item.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa Survivors and bereaved families of the November 20 boat tragedy in Bayelsa State have recounted their horrifying experiences, describing how passengers struggled for survival as the overloaded vessel capsized, leaving several people, including children, dead. The boat was conveying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie Community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state for a burial ceremony when the tragedy occurred. One of the survivors, Mrs Lucy Africanist Olugbo, an indigene of Ijo-Gbanraun who is married in Ukubie, described the ill-fated vessel as an old boat that was unfit to carry the large number of passengers. Olugbo, who was travelling to attend the burial of her husband’s half-sister, said the passengers had initially expected to travel in a speedboat, but when none was available, a local boat was brought to convey them. She said the boat started making cracking sounds shortly after boarding, raising fears among some passengers. According to her, the vessel began tilting from one side to another, forcing passengers to shift their weight in the same direction and further destabilising it. She said water had started entering the boat while it was still moving, creating panic among the passengers. Recounting how she escaped, Olugbo said she secured a bag around her neck before pushing a heavy-set woman forward and jumping into the river. She said when she resurfaced, she saw men, women and children struggling desperately in the water. The survivor also alleged that some youths who arrived in boats, apparently to assist in the rescue operation, were more interested in collecting passengers’ phones, money, bags and other belongings than rescuing those struggling in the water. She said she personally witnessed four elderly women and a young lady die in the incident. Another survivor, Mrs Mary Silas, said she travelled with seven members of her household, including her children, younger sister and younger brother. Silas said she was particularly worried because one of her sons could not swim, prompting her to approach the boat driver and appeal to him to stop and allow some passengers to disembark. She said, “The boat was shaking and making strange sounds. Because I was travelling with my son who could not swim, I became very worried. “I approached the driver and told him that there were many children and people who could not swim on board. I told him that since we were close to the riverbank, he should stop and allow some people to come down. “He told me, ‘Okay, madam, I have heard you.’ But to my surprise, instead of stopping, he sped into the middle of the river. People were shouting, and before we knew what was happening, the boat collapsed and started sinking.” Narrating how she managed to save herself and her children, Silas said she used her swimming skills to guide her son through the water. item.title: 2027 Presidential poll: What will influence our votes — Nigerians
item.description: *Torn between Tinubu’s reforms, Obi’s change message, Atiku’s comeback *Say, Tinubu has capacity to take bold decisions, Obi possesses good credentials, Atiku may reduce petrol price By Dayo Johnson, Regional Editor, South West The 2027 general election is barely two months away. Some of the political parties that will be on the ballot have already hit the streets campaigning. Many of the candidates are seeking to renew the mandate that was given to them in 2023. Others who didn’t make it in the last election are back again hoping to succeed this time around. The candidates are making fresh promises. The electorate, on their part, have been speaking on what will inform their choice of who to vote for during the elections and their responses reveal an electorate pulled in sharply different directions. We did not embark on data collation but randomly spoke with some Nigerians in the southwest, southeast, south south and the northern region of the country. Backers of President Bola Tinubu defend him on his capacity to push restructuring and take bold decisions, arguing that but for him the economy would have collapsed completely, even as some concede that his reforms have yet to ease hardship. But they have hope and argue that Nigeria would be better under Tinubu in the years to come. A few voices break from the Obi-Tinubu argument entirely, backing Atiku, the ADC, or local candidates on performance. In markets, campuses and government offices, a strong current of support for Peter Obi runs through everyday voters- market women, traders, students and civil servants, who point to the rising cost of living, government borrowing and hunger for change. Another powerful theme in their responses is the widespread distrust of the electoral system itself. Many voters express lack of faith in the process and expect politicians to rig and litigate rather than accept the people’s verdict, even as the spate of ongoing violence is already scaring them. Professionals frame their choices more cautiously arguing that they will be guided by candidates’ positions on sustainable development, Niger Delta equity and resource justice rather than ethnicity or party. From conviction to civic duty to indecision, the message from the streets is clear: a wary electorate is watching, and waiting to decide amidst fears of violence. Speaking, Amaebi Clarkson, a lawyer in Lagos , said: “The Campaigns have been intense, with grandiose promises. But beyond the rhetoric, Peter Obi obviously has good credentials, with proven track records to make a good pl president. I think he has good intentions for Nigeria and is better poised to positively drive the country. “However, I prefer Tinubu to be the president at this crucial time, not because he will bring any tangible development or perform any miracle. item.title: Mbah’s scorecard: How Enugu is rebuilding education, road infrastructure, healthcare, and transport sectors
item.description: By Steve Oko, Regional Editor, South East When he came on board in May 2023, many did not give him a chance, especially after many years of undelivered promises suffered Nigerian masses in the hand of their political leaders. But some did with high expectations, considering his antecedents both in private and public sectors. Three years and seven months down the line, Governor Peter Ndubuisi Mbah’s scorecard speaks for itself. No long ago, the administration unveiled 10,000 milestone achievements of the government. A critical analysis of his achievements reveals that significant progress has been recorded across all critical sectors. Since he mounted the saddle of leadership, Gov. Mbah has deliberately pursued a development driven by his disruptive innovation approach aimed at repositioning Enugu State as a leading economic hub in Nigeria. Anchored on his administration’s eight-year development vision, Mbah seeks to grow the state’s economy from approximately $4.4 billion to at least $30 billion in four to eight years, while tackling poverty through investments in critical sectors. At the heart of this vision is the recognition that sustainable economic growth cannot be achieved without adequate infrastructure, a productive agricultural sector, accessible healthcare and quality education, among others. These sectors form critical pillars of the administration’s development strategy, with interventions designed not only to address existing deficits, but also to prepare the state for emerging economic opportunities. Mbah has, at various fora, made it known to whoever cared to listen, that his administration was determined to move beyond policy pronouncements to measurable outcomes that could actually improve the living conditions of residents. Meanwhile , in x-raying Mbah’s scorecard, our analytical lens will today focus on four critical sectors: infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare and education. Education: 268 Smart Green Schools to transform learning Governor has left no one in doubt about his passion for education as veritable for transforming the society and building its economy. He has often held that no nation can develop beyond its human capital. But has proved that it was mere rhetoric. For three consecutive years, the Mbah Administration has allocated 33 per cent of its annual budget to the education sector, making it the number one priority in terms of resources allocation. Perhaps one of the most ambitious components of Governor Mbah’s development programme is the transformation of the education sector through the establishment of 268 Smart Green Schools across the 260 wards in Enugu State. It all seemed like a joke in the beginning. But they are all standing today. item.title: Sanwo-Olu urges council leaders to promote peaceful participation ahead of 2027 polls
item.description: Gov. Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State has urged chairmen and vice-chairmen of the 57 Local Government Areas (LGAs) and Local Council Development Areas (LCDAs) to promote peaceful democratic participation ahead of the 2027 general elections. Sanwo-Olu gave the charge at a retreat for council leaders held at Sheraton Hotel, Ikeja, with the theme: “Strengthening Grassroots Governance for Sustainable Development: Role of Local Governments in Nigeria’s 2027 Democratic Transition.” Represented by the Secretary to the State Government, Mrs Abimbola Salu-Hundeyin, the governor said that grassroots governance must be driven by transparency, accountability and tangible improvements in the lives of residents. He said local governments, being the closest tier of government to the people, played critical roles in addressing challenges relating to roads, waste management, primary healthcare, education, markets and security. “The true measure of governance lies in its tangible impact on citizens’ daily lives. As the tier of government closest to the people, council leaders serve as the first point of contact on critical issues affecting their communities. “Greater access to financial resources must translate into improved service delivery and visible development at the grassroots. “I therefore urge you to exercise prudence, transparency and accountability in the management of public resources and ensure that your expenditure priorities reflect the actual needs of your communities,” he said. Sanwo-Olu said that the ongoing reforms to strengthen local government autonomy under President Bola Tinubu’s administration had increased responsibilities for council leaders, requiring them to demonstrate effective resource management and deliver measurable development. He urged the councils to engage in healthy competition through projects in infrastructure, environmental sanitation, youth empowerment and social welfare. “As our administration approaches the end of its tenure, our priority is to consolidate our achievements and ensure the sustainability of the developmental initiatives we have implemented over the years. “Our local governments have a critical role to play in preserving this legacy. I commend the collaboration we have enjoyed with our councils, and I urge you to strengthen this partnership by aligning your development priorities,” he said. The governor also urged council leaders to promote civic awareness, uphold the rule of law and maintain peace and security before, during and after the 2027 elections. He, however, cautioned that election preparations must not distract them from their primary responsibilities, including providing functional healthcare centres, quality education and clean environments. Earlier, Dr Yekini Agbaje, Special Adviser to the Governor on Local Government, Chieftaincy Affairs and Rural Development, urged council leaders to champion peaceful civic engagement and democratic stability ahead of the elections. item.title: Manhunt launched for killers of NSCDC officer in Benue
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Chairman of Agatu Local Government Area of Benue State, Mr Melvin Ejeh, has vowed to ensure the arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the killing of an officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Inspector Anyebe Anya. Anya was reportedly killed by armed men who attacked him at his duty post at a checkpoint in Agatu a few days ago. The assailants were also said to have carted away his service rifle after the attack. Ejeh gave the assurance when he visited the deceased officer’s family in Otukpo to commiserate with them, describing Anya as a hardworking, honest and dedicated officer. He vowed that those behind the killing would not escape justice, assuring the bereaved family that efforts were already underway to track down and apprehend the perpetrators. “Those that killed him will not go unpunished. We will get all of them. I knew him personally. He was a very hardworking, honest man who was committed to his work. “The whole community is mourning his death. The people of Agatu are shocked and grieving over his death. “We console his family. He was a committed officer. I can assure you that we will get those involved and they will be brought to justice. There is a hunt for them already. “The entire Agatu people will not rest until he gets justice, that I can assure his family,” the chairman said. Efforts to reach the Public Relations Officer of the Benue State NSCDC Command, SC Michael Ejelikwu, for comments were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Manhunt launched for killers of NSCDC officer in Benue appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Meet Emmanuel Emegha, Chelsea’s new striking sensation who has Nigerian roots
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Chelsea’s latest attacking prospect, Emmanuel Emegha, is already giving supporters reasons to pay attention after scoring against Nottingham Forest on Friday. While the Blues trailed by two goals to nil, the 23-year-old striker, who joined Chelsea from French side Strasbourg, came off the bench to replace Danny Welbeck, found the net in the 54th and 89th minutes, and offered the Blues a lifeline in their Premier League encounter. However, his goals were not enough as Forest held unto their lead after Morgan Gibss-White had extended it immediately after, bringing the game to a 3-2 full-time result. Before the Forest clash, Emegha put Chelsea ahead at home when they hosted Leeds United last week. Unfortunately, he could not save the team from capitulating to a 1-4 defeat in the game. But beyond his growing reputation in England, Emegha has an interesting connection to Nigeria. Born in The Hague, Netherlands, to a Togolese father and a Nigerian mother, the powerful forward has West African roots. His Nigerian heritage makes him a player of interest to Nigerian football fans, particularly those following the growing number of players of Nigerian descent making waves in European football. However, Emegha has chosen to represent the Netherlands internationally. He made his senior debut against Poland in November 2025, explaining that the Netherlands is his country and that he is proud to be Dutch. Although Nigeria missed out on having him represent the Super Eagles, his progress at Chelsea gives Nigerian fans another reason to follow his career closely. At 23, Emegha has the physical presence, pace and goalscoring instincts to make an impression in English football. His latest goals against Nottingham Forest are another early signs of what he could offer Chelsea. item.title: Chelsea beaten at Nottingham Forest as poor run continues
item.description: Nottingham Forest claimed a memorable 3-2 victory over Chelsea at the City Ground on Friday night, November 27, piling further pressure on Blues manager Xabi Alonso after another disappointing performance from his side. Forest made a flying start to the encounter, taking the lead just five minutes into the game through Igor Jesus, who produced a superb volley from Daniel Muñoz’s cross to put the hosts ahead. Chelsea struggled to find their rhythm in the opening half, with Forest looking more dangerous and organised in attack. Despite enjoying more possession, the visitors failed to turn their dominance on the ball into meaningful goalscoring opportunities. The hosts doubled their advantage shortly after the restart when Morgan Gibbs-White converted from the penalty spot in the 51st minute. The penalty was awarded after Wesley Fofana brought down Liam Delap inside the Chelsea box. However, Chelsea responded three minutes later through substitute Emmanuel Emegha, who pulled one back after Pedro Neto’s effort took a deflection and fell kindly into his path. The goal briefly offered Chelsea hope of mounting a comeback, but Forest remained dangerous and restored their two-goal cushion in the 72nd minute when Gibbs-White grabbed his second of the evening. Chelsea refused to surrender, with Emegha scoring again in the 89th minute to reduce the deficit to 3-2 and set up a tense finish. However, Forest held on through the closing moments to secure all three points and condemn Chelsea to another painful defeat. The result represents another setback for Alonso, whose team have struggled for consistency in recent weeks. Chelsea’s defensive weaknesses and inability to control crucial moments once again proved costly. For Nottingham Forest, the victory provides a significant boost and a valuable reward for their determination and attacking efficiency. Chelsea must now turn their attention to their next Premier League fixture against Crystal Palace as they look to recover from another frustrating night. item.title: Nigeria’s $1bn Monthly Remittance Has Been Achieved – CBN Governor Cardoso
item.description: Nigeria has achieved its $1 billion monthly diaspora remittance target, the Central Bank of Nigeria has said. CBN Governor Olayemi Cardoso, who disclosed this at the 61st Annual Bankers’ Dinner of the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN) in Lagos on Friday, said Nigeria now targets $1.5 billion in monthly remittances by the end of the first half of 2027. “The fact that you can go abroad, put in your card, and make payment, yes, that is great convenience for everybody, great convenience. But beyond all that, one thing we should never forget — three years ago, two years ago, you couldn’t do all these things. “And what used to happen, you go somewhere, you want to make payments, you either have to pay in cash or use a card, which gets thrown away, and you’re disrespected,” he said. “What this has done, it has brought back the respect of all Nigerians abroad. “When I stood before you last year. I spoke of our ambition to increase monthly remittances to $1 billion a month. I am pleased to report that this milestone has been achieved. “We are now working towards increasing monthly remittances to $1.5 billion by the end of the first half of 2027,” Cardoso added. He commended licensed International Money Transfer Operators (IMTOs) for their efforts to strengthen transparency, invest in technology, and expand formal remittance channels, particularly across Asia. ﻿ Cardoso said that the next phase of Nigeria’s financial reforms must focus on deepening liquidity, broadening participation, and expanding the range of financial instruments available to businesses and investors. “The naira has strengthened by approximately six per cent over the past year, while daily foreign exchange market turnover has at times exceeded $1 billion. “In the fixed income market, daily turnover averages N1.5 trillion, supported by a credible tradable benchmark yield curve extending to 10 years. “What, what does all this mean? It is an encouraging sign of growing market confidence. The market deepens; more activity takes place when there’s confidence in the market,” he said. According to him, the priority is to ensure that markets continue to support efficient price discovery and capital allocation. “As recent movements in the foreign exchange market remind us, a well-functioning market does not mean that prices remain static. It does not mean that prices remain static. “They go up, they come down. Volatility is an inherent feature of global financial markets, and a market-determined exchange rate must be allowed to move in both directions in response to macroeconomic fundamentals and global development. “Emerging market currencies, including ours, have experienced volatility amidst changes in the United States’ interest rate environment and global risk sentiment. “Nigeria, as I have said, is part of this interconnected global financial system, but believe me, we are considerably better equipped to manage external shocks than we were three years ago.” According to him,

item.title: A Weekend For Proof
item.description: INEC tests its systems on Saturday. Opposition leaders face their own test on Monday. Campaign violence makes both exercises more consequential. By Tuesday, Nigerians should have fresh evidence about two institutions seeking their confidence. INEC will have conducted its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise. Opposition parties will have had their scheduled opportunity to formalise cooperation in Abuja. The first must demonstrate operational readiness. The second must demonstrate an ability to act together. Both approach those tests amid a worsening concern: whether citizens can participate in the campaign safely. Wednesday’s attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City, Edo State, confirmed by the police, followed Monday’s deadly violence in Delta. Edo police reported one person injured and ordered an investigation. The attackers’ political affiliations and any sponsors have not been established. That development changes the context of the coming days. Electoral preparation now requires visible progress on protection, accountability and public confidence alongside equipment and political agreements. Saturday: Let The Test Produce Evidence INEC’s mock exercise is scheduled for November 28, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time, in 17,676 selected polling units. It will test accreditation, election devices, and the uploading and viewing of simulated results. Registered voters in the selected units are expected to participate. The most useful outcome would be a public account of performance. How many locations opened on time? How many participants were successfully accredited? Where did devices fail? How long did uploads take? How were exceptions resolved? A rehearsal can reveal problems that announcements cannot. Finding a fault early allows INEC to correct it. Explaining that correction gives citizens a reason to have greater confidence. The exercise also has practical support from state governments. Lagos has cancelled Saturday’s sanitation exercise, while Anambra has postponed its own, to avoid obstructing participation. Those decisions remove an immediate obstacle. The remaining test concerns delivery at the selected polling units. Monday: What Will Opposition Unity Require? Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Seyi Makinde and other opposition leaders are expected at the November 30 summit. Their attendance and any signed commitments remain forthcoming. The APC says it is untroubled by the proposed gathering. The parties’ task is to define cooperation precisely. Joint election monitoring could be valuable. So could common procedures for documenting intimidation, sharing verified information and coordinating legal responses. Presidential cooperation presents more difficult choices. Supporters need to know whether their parties intend to campaign separately, endorse an existing candidate or pursue another lawful arrangement. A declaration of unity leaves those questions open unless it specifies obligations.

item.title: Osun LG Crisis Will Be Fully Resolved In The Next One Week — Gov Adeleke
item.description: Governor Ademola Adeleke has assured the people of Osun State that the protracted local government crisis in the state will be resolved within the next week, following President Bola Tinubu’s intervention. Governor Adeleke gave this assurance in his inaugural speech during his second-term inauguration held at Osogbo City Stadium, where he listed some of the priorities of his second-term administration across all sectors. “I am glad to announce that Mr President has intervened in the local government matter and in the next one week, the crisis will be fully resolved. Once this is done, our administration will ensure the rehabilitation of the remaining 102 primary health care centres,” he said. Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke was sworn in as governor for a second term on November 27, 2026. Photo: Femi Ojomo/Channels Television. As part of his priorities, the re-elected governor promised to set up the Osun State Electricity Regulatory Commission, as well as infrastructural expansion and recruitment of teachers and rehabilitation of schools, including reviving technical colleges. He also said that job and wealth creation will be at the heart of his second term. “We will establish a digital hub in each of our three senatorial districts. This is to drive job creation in the digital economy,” Adeleke said. “In education, we will recruit more teachers and speed up school rehabilitation. We will expand bursaries and scholarships, keep tuition affordable, tackle cultism, and revive our technical colleges.” In the health sector, he said about 70 per cent of existing primary health care centres were rehabilitated and equipped with solar and power facilities in his first term. “We upgraded and completed 232 out of 332 primary health care centres. The plan was to complete the whole 332 PHCs, but the seizure of local government allocations halted the process,” the governor said. “My government made sure that our primary school teachers, healthcare professionals at our primary healthcare centres, and local government retirees got paid in the last two years.” Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke sworn in as governor for a second term on November 27, 2026. Photo: Femi Ojomo/Channels Television. Adeleke said his vision is to move Osun from a civil service economy to an industrialised one, noting that his administration is open to partnership with private organisations and economic advisory groups. “Specifically, we will target agro-processing factories, industrial parks across districts, free trade zones, sports and tourism development, and a better business environment. “Fellow citizens, we must heal the wounds of the past and unite for our collective good. I charge the Osun political class to embrace elite consensus, transparency, good governance and local content,” he added. President Tinubu was represented at the inauguration by the Vice President, Kashim Shettima.
